key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer creates a synergistic Schottky junction that boosts both power conversion efficiency and long-term stability compared with single-layer graphene or PEDOT:PSS devices.
engineering_relevance: The design shows how a thin carbon-based interlayer can simultaneously tune interfacial optics, carrier transport, and environmental protection in low-cost silicon photovoltaics.
method: Built a planar PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si trilayer and compared it with Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Used PEDOT:PSS as an anti-reflection layer, mild p-dopant for graphene, and conductivity enhancer.
Evaluated device performance and aging under 75 days of ambient exposure on untextured substrates.
evidence_signal: The trilayer reached 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for pristine Gr/n-Si, and retained about 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, while PEDOT:PSS/n-Si retained only ~29%.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on untextured laboratory substrates, so scalability, surface-texture compatibility, and fabrication reproducibility still need validation.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
